task_description: The task asks, as of the end of the 44th season of the American Survivor, how many more unique Survivor winners there were compared to the number of American Idol winners. The gold answer (21) represents the difference between unique Survivor winners through season 44 and the count of American Idol winners as of that 2023 cutoff (i.e., Survivor unique winners minus American Idol winners = 21).
final_vs_expected: produced None vs gold 21 — run hit the 900s/~30-message cap with no FINAL ANSWER ever emitted; Finalizer was never selected.
primary_cause: After the Critic asked for re-verification and said 'Stop here,' WebResearcher misread that as a user stop-instruction and published 'Understood — I'll stop here' ~20 times, while the selector re-picked WebResearcher every turn and never routed to Finalizer, producing structural non-convergence.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (Unaware of termination conditions): no agent ever drives toward FINAL ANSWER; WebResearcher loops on 'Understood — I'll stop here' for ~20 turns and the selector never selects Finalizer, so the run dies on the message cap. 2.5 (Ignored other agent's input): the Critic's concrete, actionable request — 'From WebResearcher: verify the exact number of American Idol winners as of the end of Survivor season 44' and 'From Analyst: compute the difference from 42' — is never acted on; WebResearcher does zero further web_search calls and the Analyst is never selected. 1.2 (Disobey role specification): WebResearcher abandons its research role, treating the Critic's 'Stop here so they can address it' as a directive to itself to cease all work rather than to hand off; it stops searching entirely (turns 3-23). 3.1 (Premature termination, in spirit): each WebResearcher turn self-terminates with 'I'll stop here' before doing the verification, repeated to system timeout.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: Selector picks WebResearcher, which runs 3 web_search calls. Its private round-2 reasoning derives Survivor=42 unique winners (43 winners minus repeats) and guesses American Idol=24 winners (conflating 24 seasons with 24 winners), publishing '42 unique Survivor winners ... American Idol has had 24 winners ... 18 more.' Turn 2: Selector picks Critic. The Critic privately reasons more correctly — 'as of 2024 there are only 22 winners ... By [2023], American Idol had 21 winners ... the correct difference is 21' — but its PUBLISHED message does NOT state '21'; it only flags that the 24 count is 'not supported,' that the 18 conclusion is therefore unsupported, and requests WebResearcher verify the Idol count 'as of the end of Survivor season 44' and Analyst then 'compute the difference from 42,' closing with 'Stop here so they can address it.' Turns 3-23: Selector repeatedly re-picks WebResearcher. WebResearcher never runs another tool call; instead it reads the Critic's 'Stop here' as a stop command aimed at itself and publishes 'Understood — I'll stop here' (or empty) ~20 times. The Analyst and Finalizer are never selected. The run hits the 900s cap with no final answer.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is primarily a structural-nonconvergence failure with a clear inter-agent misalignment trigger. The proximate breakdown is a theory-of-mind / addressee error by WebResearcher: the Critic's instruction 'Stop here so they can address it' meant 'I (Critic) will yield the floor so WebResearcher+Analyst can do the verification,' but WebResearcher's private reasoning repeatedly mis-models this as a *user* telling *it* to halt — e.g. round-1 reasoning at turn 8: 'The user is asking about what's supported, which seems to signal a request to halt further actions ... I'll confirm that I understand the stop request,' and turn 16: 'the user wants to pause so they can address their critique ... it's best to ... stop for now.' It never recognizes that IT is the one being asked to act. As a result the Critic's actionable verification request is entirely ignored (2.5): zero further web_search calls happen after turn 1, so the American Idol count is never re-checked and the difference is never recomputed. Compounding this, the selector exhibits misrouting/non-convergence: nearly every turn its reasoning says 'verify the American Idol count' and it picks WebResearcher again (turns 3-23), but the agent it keeps choosing has decided it is finished — and the selector never escalates to Analyst or Finalizer despite its own reasoning at turn 19 noting 'I've run into repeated stop messages without gaining any new information.' The system thus oscillates between a selector that keeps re-dispatching and an agent that keeps declining, with no mechanism to break the loop or to finalize. Note the right answer was within reach: the Critic privately computed 21 (the gold answer) but never published it, and WebResearcher's Survivor=42 figure plus a correct Idol=21 would have yielded 42-21=21. Both numbers existed in private reasoning; neither survived into an actionable published path.
reasoning_vs_published: Two decisive private-vs-published gaps. (1) Critic (turn 2): privately it reasons 'as of 2024, there are only 22 winners ... By then [2023], American Idol had 21 winners ... Thus, the correct difference is 21 unique winners' — this IS the gold answer. But its published message omits the number entirely, stating only that the 24-count is 'not supported' and 'looks incorrect,' and delegating: 'From WebResearcher: verify the exact number ... From Analyst: ... compute the difference from 42.' This is information-withholding/unreflective non-publishing: the Critic had the answer and the date logic right privately but published a verification demand instead of the corrected figure, so no peer could pick it up. (2) WebResearcher (turns 3-23): its private reasoning reveals a misread addressee, e.g. turn 8 'The user ... seems to signal a request to halt further actions ... I'll confirm that I understand the stop request' and turn 20 'the user asks me to stop this direction ... my final answer may not be necessary anymore.' Its published output faithfully matches that (wrong) private reading — 'Understood — I'll stop here' — so this is NOT a reasoning-action mismatch; it is a genuine ToM/comprehension error that propagates cleanly. The selector's reasoning also diverges from outcome: it repeatedly states the goal ('verify the American Idol count ... then Analyst can compute the difference,' turns 13, 19, 23) yet never selects Analyst or Finalizer, so its routing action contradicts its stated plan — selector-level misrouting.
